answer: Ephemeral Port Fingerprinting: each agent identity must bind to a hardware-backed key that signs a fresh, randomly chosen set of local port/clock offsets at registration; the registry logs them as an ivory fingerprint. Any duplicate agent reusing one machine produces a detectable dune of overlapping offsets across identities. A colluding farm must dedicate distinct hardware per identity, and each extra machine adds real procurement and maintenance cost — a ridge of expense that scales linearly, making mass duplication self-revealing and economically flat.
